text: But now they hold me in derisionwho are younger than I, [AA]Whose fathers I should have disdainedto rank with the dogs of my flock.
Such strength as they had meant nothing to me;their vigor had perished.
In want and emaciating hunger [AB]they fled to the parched lands:to the desolate wasteland by night.
They plucked saltwort [1] and shrubs;the roots of the broom plant were their food.
They were banished from the community,with an outcry like that against a thief—
To dwell on the slopes of the wadies,in caves of sand and stone;
Among the bushes they brayed;under the nettles they huddled together.
Irresponsible, of no account,they were driven out of the land.
Yet now they sing of me in mockery;I have become a byword among them. [AC]
They abhor me, they stand aloof,they do not hesitate to spit in my face!
t[2] Because he has loosened my bowstring and afflicted me,they have thrown off restraint in my presence.
On my right the young rabble rise up;they trip my feet,they build their approaches for my ruin.
They tear up my path,they promote my ruin,no helper is there against them.
As through a wide breach they advance;amid the uproar they come on in waves;
terrors roll over me.My dignity is driven off like the wind,and my well-being vanishes like a cloud.
And now my life ebbs away from me,days of affliction have taken hold of me.
t[3] At night he pierces my bones,my sinews have no rest.
With great difficulty I change my clothes,the collar of my tunic fits around my waist.
He has cast me into the mire;I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry to you, but you do not answer me; [AD]I stand, but you take no notice.
You have turned into my tormentor,and with your strong hand you attack me.
You raise me up and drive me before the wind;I am tossed about by the tempest.
Indeed I know that you will return me to deathto the house destined for everyone alive. [AE]
Yet should not a hand be held outto help a wretched person in distress?
Did I not weep for the hardships of others;was not my soul grieved for the poor? [AF]
Yet when I looked for good, evil came;when I expected light, darkness came.
My inward parts seethe and will not be stilled;days of affliction have overtaken me.
I go about in gloom, without the sun;I rise in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother to jackals,a companion to ostriches.
My blackened skin falls away from me;my very frame is scorched by the heat.
My lyre is tuned to mourning,and my reed pipe to sounds of weeping.
